messages.content: I have the three flight prices now. Can you compare the real trip cost, not just airfare? The options are $936 through SAV with a connection both ways, $1,148 with a nonstop down and one stop back, or $812 through Atlanta.

Yes. I’ll compare time on the ground, baggage, connection risk, and the transportation needed after landing. Is the $812 Atlanta itinerary the one arriving after midnight Thursday, with Savannah still about a three-and-a-half-hour drive away?
That’s the one. The $936 SAV flight gets in at 8:42 Thursday night and returns at 7:55 Tuesday night. Carry-ons are included, but checking one bag each adds $140 total round trip.

Then the $936 SAV option is the middle ground. You would reach the hotel around 9:30-10:00 p.m. Thursday, so the first night is mostly lost, but Friday through Tuesday remains usable. It has two connection points across the round trip, and the working total is $3,317 with carry-ons or $3,457 with two checked bags. That leaves $483 or $343 under the $3,800 ceiling.
How does the $1,148 pairing change that?

It adds $212 over the $936 fare. The nonstop outbound removes the Thursday connection exposure and should get you to Savannah early enough for dinner and a normal first evening. The return still has one connection. Using the same lodging, downtown rideshare, three-day rental, fuel, and parking estimates, the trip totals about $3,529 before any checked-bag charge not already included, leaving $271.
So it buys us more of Thursday, but not much room if the hotels move.

Correct. A $100 lodging increase would reduce the remaining cushion to $171, and any bag fees would reduce it further. It is the easiest travel day of the three choices, but it puts the beachfront portion closest to the budget limit.
Run the Atlanta one all the way through. The $812 headline is tempting.

The airfare saves $124 versus the $936 SAV itinerary, but the ground plan gives most of that back. Because the flight arrives after midnight, driving straight through would put you in Savannah around 4:00-4:30 a.m. Friday. The more workable version adds an Atlanta airport hotel Thursday, then a Friday drive, a longer rental period, airport fees, additional fuel, and roughly seven hours of round-trip driving. I estimate $185 for the airport night and about $190 more in rental, fuel, and fees, putting the trip near $3,652. It also effectively sacrifices Thursday night and part of Friday morning.
And there is still a connection through Atlanta on the flight itself, right?

Yes. That itinerary has a connection on the outbound before the late Atlanta arrival, and the return carries similar disruption exposure. It combines the most flight complexity with the longest ground transfer, despite having the lowest airfare.
We can do carry-ons for this trip. Pick one. I don’t want to spend $212 just to recover a few hours Thursday, but I also don’t want the Atlanta drive.

Choose the $936 SAV round trip and travel with carry-ons. It keeps both airports in Savannah, avoids the overnight Atlanta stop and seven hours of extra driving, and preserves four full days plus most of Tuesday. Keep the two Savannah nights and three Tybee nights as planned: the revised transportation-and-lodging total is about $3,317, leaving $483 for fare or hotel movement. The tradeoff is a late Thursday arrival and one connection each way, but it is the best balance of usable trip time, disruption exposure, and budget. Nothing is ready to book, so I’m treating this as the selected comparison route only.
